Web-enabled Chat can now accept a model-requested lookup on any topic. Removed the keyword classifier that gated both search availability and execution: “look it up” could be missed, while “binary search tree” could trigger an unwanted search. There was no iPhone-specific production condition.

Web on offers a short optional lookup contract; it does not force every message to search. A model can answer directly in one pass without network work. Follow-up searches use the actual conversation, and custom system instructions retain the enabled web capability. Web off and developer raw mode still block lookups. Duplicate searches and repeated lookup loops remain bounded; thinking text never executes a tool.

The Guide now explains this behavior and the current DuckDuckGo Lite/Bing RSS provider path. Native model sampling, thinking controls, model loading and Chisel's tools and permissions are unchanged.

Validation: 167 frontend tests passed, including mounted Chat tests for non-iPhone requests, zero-search direct replies, follow-ups, custom instructions, Web off, raw mode, model-requested source reads, duplicate suppression, failure reporting and source persistence. Six of these checks reproduced failures before the fix. Three live provider queries also returned results without loading or querying any model. See [the web handoff review](https://github.com/UnnamedCoder-568/Uncloud/blob/main/qa/web-handoff-review-2026-10-15.md) for measurements and limitations. This is not a claim of universal model judgment or faster destination-page reading.
